title: Logit Lens vs Tuned Lens Disagreement as a Deception Smoke Detector

original_idea.body:
# Logit Lens vs Tuned Lens Disagreement as a Deception Smoke Detector

**Problem:** No one has asked whether the magnitude of logit-lens/tuned-lens disagreement is systematically larger on prompts where a model is being evasive.

**Direction:** On an open instruct model, compute per-layer logit-lens and tuned-lens distributions for factual vs refusal/hedging prompt sets. Measure layerwise KL divergence and test whether disagreement is elevated on the evasive set.

**Why it matters:** Detecting when surface behavior diverges from internal trajectory is a core safety goal (monitoring for deception/sandbagging).

**Relevant context:** Belrose et al. 2023 tuned lens; pretrained tuned-lens checkpoints exist for GPT-2 and Pythia.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: a cheap deception/sandbagging smoke detector serves a core safety-monitoring goal.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Uses pretrained tuned-lens checkpoints + KL divergence; guided, no training, mentor helpful for setup.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Tightly scoped: lens-disagreement KL on factual vs evasive prompt sets, clear hypothesis test.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Uses existing public lenses, no lab access; independent-friendly monitoring primitive.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference + two lenses on small models; low-GPU/CPU feasible.

novelty.reasoning: Using lens disagreement as a deception proxy appears not directly studied.
